paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The changes in Efficacytop (the rate of successfully maximizing the object's probability) and noise_E with the number of edits. The top figure displays results for GPT2-XL using AlphaEdit and MEMIT, while the bottom figure shows results for LLaMA3-8B using only AlphaEdit. MEMIT is excluded for LLaMA3-8B due to its excessively high noise_E, making visualization difficult.

model_annotations.German: The plot titled "GPT2-XL" illustrates the changes in two metrics, Efficacy_top and noise_E, across varying numbers of edits using two methods, AlphaEdit and MEMIT. The x-axis represents the number of edits on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 200 to 3000, with numeric tick labels spaced at regular intervals of 500 from 500 to 3000. The primary y-axis on the left is labeled "Efficacy_top" and uses a linear scale ranging from 30 to 100, featuring tick labels at intervals of 10. A secondary y-axis on the right is labeled "noise_E" and uses a linear scale with a value range from 0 to 140, featuring tick labels at intervals of 20. Four lines are plotted on the graph. The AlphaEdit Efficacy_top is represented by a dashed light red line with square markers and corresponds to the left y-axis; it starts at approximately 99 at the first data point near x=200, remains relatively steady before slowly declining, and ends at approximately 86 at x=3000. The MEMIT Efficacy_top is shown as a dashed light blue line with square markers, also corresponding to the left y-axis; it begins at approximately 88 near x=200 and exhibits a continuous downward trend, ending at a low of approximately 26 at x=3000. The AlphaEdit noise_E is depicted by a solid light red line with circular markers, corresponding to the right y-axis; it starts at approximately 2 near x=200 and displays a very gradual, steady increase to end at roughly 12 at x=3000. Finally, the MEMIT noise_E is represented by a solid light blue line with circular markers, corresponding to the right y-axis; it begins at approximately 8 near x=200 and shows a consistent upward trend across the entire x-axis, ending at a peak value of roughly 148 at x=3000.
